posts.author: Renchu
posts.body:
Hey everyone!
My game has a lot of small maps, so I decided to look for a plugin that kept the game's camera fixed in a determined place, no matter where the player's walking at the moment.
I tried using
Galv's MZ Cam Control
, and it was really good up to a certain point because it can lock the camera to a X,Y coordinate. BUT. Unfortunately, it comes with a compulsory sliding motion, and it also doesn't have the option of locking the camera to a certain axis (X
or
Y instead of only "X,Y").
Can someone help me out, please?

posts.author: Renchu

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
I didn't use this plugin yet, but to me it looks like scroll limits overlap.
Since you can set the min and max coordinates ...
<minX:#>
<maxX:#>
<minY:#>
<maxY:#>
... I'd assume, the set values push each other out of bounds. For example, if the minY tries to be 2 from the top, but the maxY also tries to be 2 from the bottom, and they cannot both be true.
Did you try to set other min/max values?

Yes, I tried. ^^;
I also increased the size of the map and tried to keep the camera centered, but unfortunately this issue doesn't seem to be the case...
However, I have good news! At least I managed to remove the sliding motion from Galv's plugin by myself -- I just had to delete the
Game_Map.prototype.updateScroll
part. This is not what's going to stop me from using it in my game anymore.
The problem with the Y axis when I use the other plugin is still very puzzling, though
EDIT:
Tested the game in a big map and turns out deleting the
Game_Map.prototype.updateScroll
part of the plugin causes the camera to completely stop moving. Oops!
But no worries, I found an
excellent plugin
that does exactly everything I need. This one quite literally saved the life of my entire project!

posts.author: Eternidade_1
posts.body:
Why not make a map the size of your screen, so the camera won't move. Or if you display an image over the map the size of your screen, you won't see the player wherever they are.
If you want to show a scene on the map, you can move the camera there and then back, which is exactly how we display large structures that can't be seen on the whole screen.
